social.hook: A Friday night in Anaheim, 23 years back in the books.
social.caption: Joe Jackson at House of Blues Anaheim on August 29, 2003 — now 23 years in the archive. The full entry is on the site.
beats: August 29, 2003: a Friday night at House of Blues Anaheim.
Joe Jackson, a room built for exactly this kind of show.
Twenty-three years later, it still holds a place in the archive.
The record is on the site. That night is not going anywhere.

social.hook: Ten years of sitting with that night.
social.caption: The Smithereens at the Birchmere ten years ago today — still in the archive, still worth the revisit. Some rooms and some bands are just right for each other.
beats: Ten years ago tonight I was in a seat at the Birchmere in Alexandria.
The Smithereens played, and the Birchmere is exactly the kind of room built for a band like that.
August 26, 2016 is in the archive — the date, the place, the fact of being there.
A decade out, the entry still holds. That's what the archive is for.

social.hook: Twenty-three years later, I still have the ticket stub.
social.caption: The Human League at The Grove of Anaheim, August 24, 2003 — it's in the archive now. Twenty-three years is a long time to keep a stub, but some nights earn the drawer space.
beats: August 24, 2003: The Human League played The Grove of Anaheim on a summer Sunday night.
The Grove was a mid-size outdoor venue that suited a band built for big, clean sound.
By 2003, 'Don't You Want Me' was already more than twenty years old and still stopped the room.
The ticket stub went into the collection that night and stayed there — which is how a show makes it into the archive.
Twenty-three years on, the entry is live. The record is the point.

social.hook: Forty-one summers back, a Friday night in August that's still in the log.
social.caption: August 23, 1985: New Order at Irvine Meadows, and it's been in the archive ever since. Forty-one years later, the entry still stands.
beats: August 23, 1985 — a Friday night at an outdoor amphitheater in Irvine, California.
New Order were deep into the Low-life era, the album having arrived just three months before this show.
Irvine Meadows was the kind of open-air room that made a band sound both enormous and close at the same time.
Forty-one years in the log. The date holds.
